name: b472_s1b
headline: Human Written
windows: One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is influence literacy: an increased awareness of all the ways your attention is being shaped in your day-to-day life (a screen, a specific ad, a politician, religious fear, erotic imprinting, charismatic authority, pressure to belong, shame, a sense of urgency, repetition, etc.).

Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.
Manipulation often comes with any of the following; urgency, you are special, FOMO (fear of missing out), not be included, sexual charge, shame, confused, someone will rescue you, destiny, you should obey, secret knowledge, and an excessive sense of certainty about something way too quickly and you have a sense that one good question will break the spell.

name: b472_s2b
headline: AI Generated
windows:
To turn this off, stop rehearsing it, take it out of any recordings that you have, stop having it in any apps that are active, and go back to using your regular induction that you have been using. Say that you won’t use it anymore when you are awake, but realize that just saying that it is gone won’t make it go away immediately. If you are finding that you are responding to it when you don’t want to, or you are having problems with being disoriented after using it, get some help from someone who is qualified to help you. If you want to keep it in, you can, but only for the use of starting a session at a later time when you want to. For now, today’s trance will be over when you come out of it.
As you come back, undo anything you did to change your state on the way in. So if you floated, come back down and regain your weight (of your choice, of course). If you shrank, grow back to your normal size. If you went younger or met parts, come back to feeling all of you here and now, in a body that’s yours, with your adult mind in charge of it. If you went off somewhere, come back the same way you went. Etcetera. Only bring out with you the things you actually want to bring.

name: b472_s3b
headline: Human Written
windows: Then count up, using these five steps: 1...feel your body again and what it’s resting on, feel your weight (of your choice). 2...feel your breathing return to normal. 3...hear the room, name where you are. 4...wiggle your fingers and toes, move your shoulders and your eyes. 5...open your eyes, back in the here and now, feeling normal and clear.

When you come out, remind yourself what day (or date) it is. Look to your left and your right. Look at something near, and something far. Move around a bit, and don’t get up until you feel steady. Make sure you’re actually oriented and alert (the count is supposed to bring you back, but it doesn’t always do the whole job). Take mental note of anything that has come up for you and any actions you need to take regarding it.
Then go on and do something normal.
